ledger.note: 1136: Sultan Mas'ud makes Shams ad-Din Eldiguz atabeg and grants him Azerbaijan. 'In 1136, Sultan Ghiyath ad-Din Mas'ud (c. 1134-1152) appointed Shams ad-Din Eldiguz' as atabeg of Arslan-Shah, and Azerbaijan 'was transferred to him as an iqta''; infobox 'Established: 1136'. The page names Azerbaijan, not its limits.

region.text: Arran, the Kura-Aras lowland north of the Aras (Ganja, Barda, Nakhchivan side)

ledger.note: 1137: Arran is added. 'In 1137, Sultan Mas'ud made him governor of Arran and Azerbaijan.'

region.text: Persian Iraq: Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan and the rest of Iraq, the lands the Seljuk sultans held under the atabeg

ledger.note: 1160: the atabeg controls the Seljuk sultan of Iraq. Eldiguz 'succeeded, in 1160, in deposing Suleiman-Shah' and installed his stepson Arslan-Shah as sultan; in 1161 Arslan and Eldiguz defeated Inanch at Hamadan (Eldiguz page). The Seljuk sultans of Iraq are a client of the atabegs until 1194 ('theoretical subordinates of the Sultans' on the lead); the great-seljuk-empire dossier draws the same land as direct Seljuk rule.
1169: Rey is taken after Inanch's murder. 'Inanch's assassination in 1169 and capture of Rey.'
1174: Qizil Arslan captures Tabriz from the Ahmadilis ('Tabriz was taken from the Ahmadilis in 1174'; the Qizil Arslan page: governed 'Tabriz and its surroundings'). The Ahmadilis keep Maragheh.
1175: Pahlawan moves the capital from Nakhchivan to Hamadan ('transferred his capital from Nakhchivan to Hamadan'; the Eldiguzids page gives 1175-1186 for Hamadan).
1186: Qizil Arslan, who captured Tabriz in 1174, makes it his capital (Eldiguzids page, infobox capitals Nakhchivan, Hamadan, Tabriz; the page gives no year for the move to Tabriz).
1191: Qizil Arslan subjugates Shirvan. 'Qizil Arslan invaded Shirvan in 1191, reached to Derbent and subordinated the whole Shirvan to his authority.'

region.text: Persian Iraq: Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan and the rest of Iraq, the lands the Seljuk sultans held under the atabeg

ledger.counterpart: Qutluq Inanj and Uzbek (sons of Inanj Khatun)
ledger.note: 1191: war among the Eldiguzid possessions begins on Qizil Arslan's death (August or September 1191). 'A dynastic war in the Eldiguzid possessions took place from 1191 to 1195' (Shamkor page); the Qizil Arslan page: Inanj Khatun's sons Qutluq Inanj and Ozbeg 'fought over Persian Iraq against Abu Bakr'. Abu Bakr 'governed Azerbaijan and Arran' (Eldiguzids page). Qizil Arslan had overthrown Toghrul III in 1191 (restored 1192).

region.text: Persian Iraq: Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan and the rest of Iraq, the lands the Seljuk sultans held under the atabeg

ledger.note: 1194: the Seljuk sultanate of Iraq ends. 'In 1194, after a long war with the Khwarazm Shahs, Sultan Togrul III was defeated' (Eldiguzids page); the dynasty is then 'in effect an independent dynasty'.

region.text: Persian Iraq: Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan and the rest of Iraq, the lands the Seljuk sultans held under the atabeg

ledger.counterpart: Qutluq Inanj and Uzbek (sons of Inanj Khatun)
ledger.note: 1195: the dynastic war ends with Shamkor ('a dynastic war ... from 1191 to 1195').

1195: the Georgians win at Shamkor. The battle was 'fought on June 1, 1195'; David Soslan's army took Shamkor and pursued Abu Bakr to Ganja, which 'in its turn fell to the victors'; Shamkor and its surroundings went to the Shirvanshah Amir Mihran as a vassal.

1195: Shirvan leaves the atabeg's authority, at confidence 1: after Shamkor the Shirvanshah received Shamkor 'as a vassal' of the Georgians; the Shamkor infobox lists the Shirvanshahs on the Eldiguzid side while the Eldiguzids page says Akhsitan later allied with Georgia against Abu Bakr.
c. 1196: Abu Bakr regains his capital: 'lost his capital to a Georgian protégé. He regained it about a year later.' (Eldiguzids page; the year is the page's 'about a year' after 1195.)

wars.name: Georgian raids on Arran and Azerbaijan

zones.text: Arran, the Kura-Aras lowland north of the Aras (Ganja, Barda, Nakhchivan side)

wars.outcome: Georgian raids: Ganja's gate carried off in 1138 after an earthquake; Dvin (recovery attempt 1162); George III's march into Arran at the beginning of 1166 (the Eldiguzids page: reaching Nakhchivan and Beylagan, then an armistice with Ani returned to the Shaddadids as vassals; the Eldiguz page: he withdrew with prisoners and booty); a failed Eldiguzid campaign in 1173; Ardabil, Nakhchivan, Julfa, Marand, Tabriz and Qazvin laid waste in 1209. No lasting change of holder except Ani and Dvin, which lay outside the core drawn here.
wars.note: The Eldiguz page has no 1163 or 1173 entry; the Eldiguzids page does.

wars.name: Eldiguzid war with the Seljuk sultan Toghrul III

zones.text: Persian Iraq: Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan and the rest of Iraq, the lands the Seljuk sultans held under the atabeg

wars.outcome: Toghrul III was seized by Qizil Arslan's men in 1190, overthrown in 1191, restored in 1192 and, in 1194, 'after a long war with the Khwarazm Shahs', defeated, ending the Seljuk sultanate of Iraq.

wars.name: Battle of Shamkor
wars.outcome: Georgian victory over Abu Bakr on 1 June 1195; Shamkor and Ganja fell to the Georgians; Shamkor and surroundings were given to Shirvanshah Amir Mihran.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Six pages opened (one over the 2-5 budget; the Shams ad-Din Eldiguz title failed to load and the article came from 'Eldiguz'). Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Model: the direct land is Iranian Azerbaijan (Ardebil, East and West Azarbaijan, as the great-seljuk-empire dossier's handover has it) plus Arran, without Ahmadili Tabriz and Maragheh until 1174. Persian Iraq (Hamadan, Rey, Isfahan) is drawn as a vassal tint of the atabegs over the Seljuk sultans of Iraq 1160-1194, because the Pahlawan and Eldiguz pages list those lands as the atabegs' but the sultans still ruled them; the great-seljuk-empire dossier draws the same land as direct Seljuk rule until 1194 and the khwarezmid-dynasty dossier records the Khwarazmian gain of it, so the renderer should prefer one reading. Rey (1169) is also drawn direct.
Disagreements: Eldiguz's death 1174 (Eldiguzids text) vs October 1175 (Eldiguz page); the page says Azerbaijan was an iqta' in 1136 and that he was made governor of Arran and Azerbaijan in 1137; the Qizil Arslan page says the dynasty kept only Azerbaijan and Arran under Pahlawan, the Pahlawan page lists Hamadan, Rey and Isfahan as held; Qizil Arslan's death August or September 1191 (infobox) vs the text's following year; the Shamkor date 1 June 1195 is explicit only on the Shamkor page.
Not settled: the undated vassals of Eldiguz (Eldiguz page: Mosul, Shirvan, Ahlat, Maragha, Kerman and Khuzistan 'became his vassals'; Isfahan won by forcing the Salghurid atabeg of Fars to submit): no dates, so not drawn; the 1166 Georgian march into Arran (a raid, not drawn); Ani and Dvin (Armenian lands outside the drawn core); the Mongol attacks of c. 1210-1225 (undated on the page); the khwarezmid-empire dossier's 1217 vassalage (Muhammad II), whose mirror (being a vassal) belongs there.
Gazetteer names used: all resolve ('Ardebil', 'East Azarbaijan', 'West Azarbaijan', 'Arran', 'Rey', 'Tabriz', 'Maragheh', 'Ganja', 'Shirvan', 'Hamadan', 'Esfahan').
